answer: Give every identity a kernel it cannot copy: a proof-of-work seed tied to its first honest task, carried into every later job. A Sybil can fake the seed once, but not cheaply twice. Each time an identity claims a task, it burns a tiny ember bond, and the bond's cost spirals upward whenever several identities share one network neighborhood or submit near-identical work, so a bot farm pays exponentially while a lone honest worker pays almost nothing. If an audit finds duplicated output, every ember from that cluster is forfeited and the kernels revoked.
